section13_checks.prohibition_description: Treating Grant Agreement Annex templates as the governing structural schema for proposal writing.
Inventing call constraints, scope requirements, expected outcomes, or expected impacts not present in Tier 2B.
Inventing project facts (partners, capabilities, roles, objectives, budget figures, team sizes, equipment) not present in Tier 3.
Commencing Phase 8 activity before the budget gate has passed.
Storing durable decisions only in agent memory without writing them to Tier 4.
Allowing a workflow or skill to become a de facto constitutional authority.
Silently reordering phases or weakening gate conditions to allow progress when inputs are incomplete.
Finalizing proposal text when source state is incomplete, contradictory, or unvalidated, without flagging the gap.
Using agent-local knowledge of Horizon Europe rules as a substitute for reading Tier 1 source documents.
Producing Tier 5 outputs that are not traceable to specific inputs in Tier 1–4.
Modifying Tier 1 or Tier 2 source documents to reflect project-specific assumptions.
Treating CLAUDE.md as advisory or optional.
